scenes.heading: Start with a name.
scenes.caption: Your app needs an address for a name before it connects.

scenes.heading: Ask the resolver.
scenes.caption: The client sends the question to its configured DNS resolver.

scenes.heading: A cached answer?
scenes.caption: The resolver may already have a usable answer in its cache.

scenes.heading: Or do a lookup.
scenes.caption: If needed, it asks other DNS servers to find the answer.

scenes.heading: Return an address.

scenes.heading: A failure is a clue.

title: DNS, in motion
summary: A simplified DNS flow: client, configured resolver, cached answer or lookup, address reply if found.
scope_note: Simplified flow. Local hosts files, client caches, record types, referrals and transport details are omitted. The example address is illustrative.
transcript: Your app needs an address for a name before it connects. The client sends the question to its configured DNS resolver. The resolver may already have a usable answer in its cache. If needed, it asks other DNS servers to find the answer. If found, the resolver replies with the requested address. Use nslookup to query a name and inspect the DNS response. Example command: nslookup app.example.com. Name resolution failure is not proof the app server is broken.
